# Now 2.13.66
- The full screen view now has the same touch feedback as the desktop overlay. Moving the pointer onto any control gives a small tick, with the same distinct feel for previous, play and next. - Swipe across the album art in full screen to change track, exactly as in the desktop overlay. The next or previous cover slides in behind your finger as you go, and the gesture springs back if you release early. It only works over the artwork itself, so swiping across the lyrics still scrolls them. - The volume slider now closes when you press any other control, including going full screen. Previously it stayed open with no way to dismiss it except returning to the desktop overlay and pressing the same button again.

# Now 2.13.65
- Line changes settle more slowly and more evenly. Every change now takes a little longer to come to rest, which reads as gentler than the same movement done quickly. The variation between a short line change and a long one has also been rebalanced: previously the distance was absorbed almost entirely by how long the change took, so some settled visibly and others seemed to arrive at once. It is now shared evenly between how long a change takes and how fast it moves, which is the closest a line change can get to feeling the same every time.

# Now 2.13.64
- A softer, calmer line change. Lines now settle a little past their resting place rather than springing well beyond it, and the lines around the one being sung move noticeably less, so a change reads as graceful rather than emphatic. The even pacing from the last version is unchanged.
